summary: H2 stream resets and growing response-trailer headers cause API gateway idle timeouts and delayed TTFB for long streaming completions
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent long tail latency and mid-stream stalls for streaming completions. Symptoms observed are delayed first byte (TTFB) spikes and eventual 504 from ALB after ~60s. Impact: ScribeLabs reports user-facing timeouts in their long-chat workflow; ~6% of streams for long responses (>4k tokens) hit the problem during peak. Observed behavior: - Client initiates streaming completion; partial bytes are emitted but the stream pauses for 20-45s with no forward progress; ALB logs show 'idle timeout' for the upstream connection. - H2 stream reset frames (RST_STREAM) appear from edge then a subsequent upstream connection is torn down; response trailers (internal metadata, e.g., x-trace, x-cache-baggage) are observed growing over the stream because of repeated per-chunk telemetry aggregation. - When trailer header size crosses ~32KB, APIGW/ALB's internal buffering triggers and combined with keepalive rotation results in connection churn and eventual idle termination.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a client that opens an HTTP/2 streaming completion to hosted API with long generation (>4k tokens).
2) Enable request tracing and attach a large set of per-chunk metadata to response trailers (simulating our internal telemetry aggregation),
3) Send steady-duration requests at ~40RPS from a single IP to reproduce header accumulation on an edge path,
4) Observe ALB access logs, edge proxy metrics (upstream_idle_timeout, h2_rst_count), and serving-runtime logs during the stalls.
logs: 2026-03-10T18:02:51Z alb[us-east-1] ERROR idle_timeout upstream_ip=10.20.3.45 target_port=8443 request_id=xyz-0001 status=504
2026-03-10T18:03:04Z serving-runtime[req=xyz-0001] INFO trailers_accumulated size=33728 bytes tokens=4120
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: header/trailer growth combined with HTTP/2 flow-control interaction causes proxy to buffer more and not flush, hitting ALB idle thresholds.
Confirmed reproduction in staging with synthetic client that appends 12-16KB of trailer metadata across the stream. Observed h2 RST at the moment trailer size exceeds ~30KB.
Edge proxy config shows brotli/content-coding disabled for these responses, but there is internal aggregation of telemetry into trailers that is unbounded under current config.
Comparing ALB logs with edge metrics shows ALB's idle timeout (default 60s) fires after the mid-stream pauses — the pause often aligns with proxy waiting for end-of-stream/trailer finalization.
Heap of upstream connection objects increases during peak; suspect backpressure due to insufficient write flush when many small chunks are coalesced into larger buffered write leading to late TTFB.
comments: Support (Maya): Customer reported increased 504s starting 2026-03-09 after a model rollout. Provided initial logs and sample request id xyz-0001.
SRE (Diego): Reproduced locally in staging with a synthetic trailer producer. Opening ticket for APIGW config review and serving-runtime change to cap trailer size.
Customer (ScribeLabs - Elena): Confirmed issue reduces when we limit per-chunk telemetry; please advise on long-term fix as we rely on embedded telemetry for observability.

SRE (Diego): Short-term mitigation applied in staging: limit aggregated trailer metadata to 8KB and enabled aggressive flush-on-chunk for HTTP/2 streams. Requesting customer to validate in prod mirror.
resolution: Mitigation applied: 1) Serving-runtime patched to cap accumulated trailer metadata to 8KB per stream and drop non-essential baggage. 2) Edge proxy configuration updated to force flush small chunks immediately for streaming responses (reduce coalescing). 3) ALB idle timeout increased from 60s to 90s for affected target group as a safety net. Post-change monitoring shows error rate for long streams dropped from 6% -> 0.5% in the test window.
follow_up_actions: Create a permanent server-side limit for trailer metadata and add per-customer quotas for aggregated telemetry (ACTION-OPS-2243)
Add an automated regression test in CI that simulates large trailer growth over HTTP/2 (ACTION-ENG-3377)
Update customer runbook and notify Dedicated customers of the configuration change and recommended telemetry settings
Evaluate long-term: consider stripping trailers on edge and sending telemetry to a sidecar path asynchronously
